name: bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data that owns bfqq, bfqq is the queue being expired (normally the in-service queue), compensate says whether the idle time is excluded from the measured service time, reason is a bfqq_expiration value; the caller is expected to hold bfqd->lock (this function itself takes and releases no lock and takes or drops no reference directly). Postcondition: returns nothing. (1) slow = bfq_bfqq_is_slow(bfqd, bfqq, compensate, &delta) with delta (milliseconds) initialised to 0. For a non-sync bfqq bfq_bfqq_is_slow returns false at once and delta stays 0. For a sync bfqq it writes delta in each of its cases: BFQ_MIN_TT/NSEC_PER_MSEC (non-rotational device) or bfq_slice_idle/NSEC_PER_MSEC (rotational device) when the measured interval is under 1000 microseconds (slow is then BFQQ_SEEKY(bfqq)), otherwise the interval in milliseconds, with slow = (bfqq->entity.service < bfq_max_budget/2) when the interval exceeds 20000 microseconds and slow = BFQQ_SEEKY(bfqq) when it is between 1000 and 20000 microseconds. The interval runs from bfqd->last_budget_start to bfqd->last_idling_start when compensate is true, otherwise to the current time. (2) Only if bfqq->wr_coeff == 1 and (slow, or reason == BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT with bfq_bfqq_budget_left(bfqq) >= entity->budget/3) it calls bfq_bfqq_charge_time(bfqd, bfqq, delta) (delta is 0 for a non-sync queue). (3) If bfqd->low_latency and wr_coeff == 1, last_wr_start_finish = jiffies. (4) If bfqd->low_latency, bfqd->bfq_wr_max_softrt_rate > 0 and bfqq->sort_list is empty: dispatched == 0 sets soft_rt_next_start = bfq_bfqq_softrt_next_start(bfqd, bfqq); dispatched > 0 marks the softrt_update flag; a negative dispatched does neither. (5) bfqd->rqs_injected and bfqd->wait_dispatch are set to false and bfqd->waited_rq to NULL. (6) __bfq_bfqq_recalc_budget(bfqd, bfqq, reason) is called, then __bfq_bfqq_expire(bfqd, bfqq, reason) (which may set the split_coop mark, removes bfqq from the busy structures or requeues it, and may free bfqq). If that returns true (bfqq is gone) the function returns immediately without touching any service field. Otherwise: if bfqq is not busy and reason is neither BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT nor BFQQE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, bfqq is marked non_blocking_wait_rq and bfqq->entity.service is left unchanged; in the else case bfqq->entity.service is set to 0. After the end of the slice (the slice ends at line 4431, right after the else branch above; the remaining statements are file lines 4432-4452, comment included), the function finishes with entity = entity->parent and entity->service = 0 applied to each entity of the for_each_entity loop starting there: with CONFIG_BFQ_GROUP_IOSCHED every ancestor up the parent chain until a NULL parent, without it at most the single entity->parent if it is non-NULL. Return points: the early return after __bfq_bfqq_expire returns true (line 4417, inside the slice) and the implicit return at the closing brace (line 4452, after the slice).
note: Reviewer claim 1 (non-sync queues can still be slow via BFQQ_SEEKY): WRONG. block/bfq-iosched.c:4154 initialises slow = BFQQ_SEEKY but 4156-4157 'if (!bfq_bfqq_sync(bfqq)) return false;' returns false before any use, so for a non-sync queue slow is false and *delta_ms is never written (delta keeps its initial 0 from 4340). Reviewer claim 2 (delta set only when compensate and interval >= 1ms): WRONG. For a sync queue delta is written on both sides of the 1 ms test (4173/4175 for interval < 1000 us, 4180 otherwise); 'compensate' only selects the interval end (4159-4162). Other fixes made: the parent-entity loop (4449-4451) description now states exactly what for_each_entity does in each config (bfq-iosched.h:1105-1106 and 1123-1124), earlier 'single level otherwise' was inexact; slow definition now spells out the three interval ranges (4167-4198); softrt branch handles dispatched<0 explicitly (4386-4395).

name: _badblocks_set
prose: Precondition: bb points to an initialised struct badblocks with a valid page table; the caller does not hold bb->lock (the function takes the write seqlock itself, saving interrupt flags); [s, s+sectors) is the range to record and acknowledged says whether the new entries are acknowledged. Postcondition: the function has these exits. (a) If bb->shift < 0 (badblocks disabled) it returns false at once, taking no lock and changing nothing. (b) If sectors == 0 it returns false at once, taking no lock and changing nothing. (c) Otherwise, if bb->shift != 0, the code evaluates rounddown(s, 1 << bb->shift) and roundup(next, 1 << bb->shift) but these macros (include/linux/math.h) expand to statement expressions, roundup(x,y) = ({ typeof(y) __y = y; (((x) + (__y - 1)) / __y) * __y; }) and rounddown(x,y) = ({ typeof(x) __x = (x); __x - (__x % (y)); }), which contain no assignment to x, so the expression value is computed and discarded, so s and next are unchanged and sectors = next - s keeps its original value: no rounding to the shift granularity takes place. Then it takes the write seqlock (irq-saving) and loops over re_insert. Each pass sets bad.start = s, bad.len = sectors and handles one piece of the range: if the table is full (badblocks_full) it jumps to out without inserting; if the table is empty it inserts the whole piece at index 0 (count + 1); otherwise it finds prev = prev_badblocks and (i) with no entry starting at or before s it inserts at index 0, trimming the piece to end before the first existing entry (count + 1); (ii) if can_combine_front, it combines p[prev-1] with p[prev] (count - 1, added); (iii) else if can_merge_front it merges into p[prev]; (iv) else if the piece overlaps p[prev], then if can_front_overwrite fails with extra > 0 (extra table slots needed) it jumps to out, and if it fails with extra <= 0 it skips min(BB_END(p[prev]) - s, sectors) sectors without changing the table, while if it succeeds it overwrites in front (count increased by extra, added) and then combines with the previous entry when possible (count - 1); (v) otherwise it inserts after prev, trimmed to end before the next entry if it overlaps that one (count + 1). After a piece, s advances and sectors decreases by the length handled; if sectors is still above 0 the loop repeats, else try_adjacent_combine(bb, prev) is called (it may merge p[prev] with p[prev+1] and decrement count; its result is ignored) and control reaches out. At out, if added != 0, set_changed(bb) is called and then, if acknowledged is 0, bb->unacked_exist = 1, else badblocks_update_acked(bb). The write seqlock is released with the saved flags and the function returns (sectors == 0), i.e. true exactly when the whole range was processed (recorded or skipped over), false when it stopped early at out because the table was full or an overwrite needed extra slots; in the early-stop case the part of the range handled before the stop stays recorded. The write seqlock is taken once and released once, at the exit after out.
note: Reviewer claim (rounddown/roundup mutate s and next so the range is rounded): WRONG. block/badblocks.c:860-861 are the calls 'rounddown(s, 1 << bb->shift); roundup(next, 1 << bb->shift);' as bare statements; include/linux/math.h:71-76 defines roundup(x,y) as a statement expression '({ typeof(y) __y = y; (((x) + (__y - 1)) / __y) * __y; })' and math.h:85-90 defines rounddown(x,y) as '({ typeof(x) __x = (x); __x - (__x % (y)); })'; both only compute a value, neither assigns to x, so s and next are not modified and line 862 'sectors = next - s' equals the original sectors. (This is a known upstream quirk of this version; the same pattern is at badblocks.c:1074-1075 and 1310-1311.) Prose now spells out the rounding no-op and enumerates all exits and each branch's count effect from the source (badblocks.c:866-980).

name: BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64)
prose: The macro invocation BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64) (accessors.h:265, macro defined at accessors.h:62-74) generates two static inline functions, each starting with a compile-time check that the member is exactly 64 bits wide: u64 btrfs_inode_size(const struct extent_buffer *eb, const struct btrfs_inode_item *s) and void btrfs_set_inode_size(const struct extent_buffer *eb, struct btrfs_inode_item *s, u64 val). Precondition: eb is a valid extent buffer and s is the offset of an inode item inside eb, represented as a pointer value (not a dereferenceable address). Postcondition, getter: it has a single return statement, return btrfs_get_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size)). With member_offset = (unsigned long)s + offsetof(size): if member_offset + 8 > eb->len, btrfs_get_64 issues a btrfs_warn bounds report and returns 0; otherwise it returns the 64-bit little-endian value stored at that offset (read across two folios when the field straddles a folio boundary). The getter does not modify the buffer. Postcondition, setter: it returns nothing and calls btrfs_set_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size), val). If member_offset + 8 > eb->len it issues the same bounds warning and writes nothing; otherwise it stores val in little-endian byte order at that offset (split across two folios when the field straddles a boundary), which modifies the extent buffer contents (the const qualifier on eb applies to the descriptor, not the data). Neither function takes a lock, takes or drops a reference, allocates memory or marks the buffer dirty.
note: Previously unreviewed (the review call failed), prose re-derived from fs/btrfs/accessors.h:62-74 (macro) and fs/btrfs/accessors.c:51-112 (DEFINE_BTRFS_SETGET_BITS: bounds check at 63-66 for get, 93-96 for set; split-folio paths 71-80 and 102-111). Wording tightened: bounds condition stated exactly (member_offset + 8 > eb->len), both single exits enumerated, no 'always/never' claims.

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: This slice starts inside btrfs_commit_transaction (function at transaction.c:2209-2646) at line 2285, in the branch taken when another task is already committing, and ends at line 2540 inside the commit proper; the lines after 2540 are described last. Precondition: trans is a handle of trans->fs_info with trans->use_count 1 (ASSERT only), cur_trans = trans->transaction; the handle is consumed by each exit of the whole function (ended with btrfs_end_transaction, or freed after the commit, or freed in the cleanup path). Four return statements exist in the whole function: 2298 (waiting branch), 2616 (successful commit), 2635 (cleanup path) and 2645 (early exits). Behaviour. (A) Waiting branch, lines 2285-2299 (taken when cur_trans->state >= COMMIT_PREP, with want_state initialised to COMPLETED at 2278): want_state = SUPER_COMMITTED if trans->in_fsync, otherwise it stays COMPLETED; the COMMIT_PREP lockdep map is released; ret = btrfs_end_transaction(trans); wait_for_commit(cur_trans, want_state); if the transaction is aborted ret is replaced by cur_trans->aborted; the extra reference on cur_trans is dropped; it returns ret. (B) Commit proper, otherwise: state = COMMIT_PREP and waiters are woken. If cur_trans is not first in fs_info->trans_list, want_state = COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED if trans->in_fsync); if the previous transaction's state is below want_state, a reference on it is taken, trans_lock is dropped, wait_for_commit(prev_trans, want_state), ret = prev_trans->aborted, the reference is put, and a non-zero ret goes to label lockdep_release; otherwise trans_lock is retaken. If cur_trans is first in the list and BTRFS_FS_ERROR is set, trans_lock is dropped and ret = -EROFS goes to lockdep_release. The state becomes COMMIT_START, trans_lock is dropped, critical_section_start_time is recorded and the external-writer count is decremented. ret = btrfs_start_delalloc_flush(fs_info) (in this tree it only starts writeback when FLUSHONCOMMIT is set and returns 0, but the result is checked): non-zero goes to lockdep_release. ret = btrfs_run_delayed_items(trans): non-zero goes to lockdep_release. The label lockdep_release (2637-2640) only releases the extwriters and writers lockdep maps and then goes to cleanup_transaction, so these three failures end in the full cleanup path described below. Then the task waits until the external writer count is 0, runs btrfs_run_delayed_items a second time (non-zero: releases the writers lockdep map and goes directly to cleanup_transaction), calls btrfs_wait_delalloc_flush (waits only when FLUSHONCOMMIT is set), waits until pending_ordered is 0, calls btrfs_scrub_pause, then under trans_lock calls add_pending_snapshot(trans) and sets state COMMIT_DOING, waits until num_writers == 1, clears BTRFS_FS_COMMIT_TRANS, and if the transaction is aborted sets ret = cur_trans->aborted and goes to scrub_continue. Then it takes reloc_mutex and runs create_pending_snapshots, btrfs_run_delayed_items, btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, U64_MAX), commit_fs_roots, btrfs_free_log_root_tree, btrfs_qgroup_account_extents (a negative result fails) and commit_cowonly_roots; any non-zero (negative for qgroup) result goes to unlock_reloc with ret set; if the transaction is aborted after that, ret = cur_trans->aborted and the path goes to unlock_reloc. It then sets cur_trans = fs_info->running_transaction, adds the tree root and chunk root to cur_trans->switch_commits, calls switch_commit_roots and update_super_roots, zeroes the super block log root and level, copies super_copy to super_for_commit, calls btrfs_commit_device_sizes, clears BTRFS_FS_LOG1_ERR and LOG2_ERR, calls btrfs_trans_release_chunk_metadata and takes tree_log_mutex (line 2539; the slice ends here). After the slice: under trans_lock state = UNBLOCKED and fs_info->running_transaction = NULL; reloc_mutex is released; btrfs_write_and_wait_transaction (failure: btrfs_handle_fs_error, tree_log_mutex released, goto scrub_continue); write_all_supers(fs_info, 0) followed by releasing tree_log_mutex (failure: goto scrub_continue, without btrfs_handle_fs_error); update_commit_stats; state SUPER_COMMITTED; btrfs_finish_extent_commit (failure: goto scrub_continue); btrfs_clear_space_info_full if HAVE_FREE_BGS; btrfs_set_last_trans_committed; state COMPLETED; the transaction is removed from fs_info->trans_list; two references on cur_trans are dropped; sb_end_intwrite if the handle is freezable; btrfs_scrub_continue; current->journal_info is cleared if it is trans; the handle is freed; it returns ret (0 at that point). Labels: unlock_reloc releases reloc_mutex and falls into scrub_continue, which calls btrfs_scrub_continue and falls into cleanup_transaction: btrfs_trans_release_metadata, btrfs_cleanup_pending_block_groups, btrfs_trans_release_chunk_metadata, trans->block_rsv = NULL, a warning 'Skipping commit of aborted transaction.', current->journal_info cleared if it is trans, then cleanup_transaction(trans, ret) (aborts the transaction with ret, removes it from the transaction list, runs btrfs_cleanup_one_transaction, clears fs_info->running_transaction if it is this transaction, drops two references, cancels scrub unless relocation is running, and frees the handle); it returns the negative errno ret. lockdep_release releases two lockdep maps then goes to cleanup_transaction (so scrub is not resumed on that path, which is correct because scrub_pause has not yet run there). The pending snapshot of trans is linked into cur_trans->pending_snapshots only by the two add_pending_snapshot calls (2280 in the waiting branch and 2393 before COMMIT_DOING): not on the early exits, and not on failures before 2393 (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delalloc flush, first or second delayed items).
note: Reviewer claim (annotation says start_delalloc_flush / first delayed_items failures go to cleanup, code jumps to lockdep_release): the jump is real but the substance is not a disagreement: transaction.c:2350-2352 and 2354-2356 'goto lockdep_release', and 2637-2640 shows the label body is two btrfs_lockdep_release calls followed by 'goto cleanup_transaction'. So those failures do end in the cleanup path (2625-2635), only through the lockdep_release label. The prose now names the label and states that it falls into cleanup_transaction. The second delayed-items failure (2369-2373) jumps directly to cleanup_transaction after one lockdep release. Verified all four returns (2298, 2616, 2635, 2645) and the scrub_continue/unlock_reloc fall-through ordering (2618-2635).

name: aio_poll_wake
prose: Function aio_poll_wake(wait, mode, sync, key) (aio.c:1787-1867), the wake callback of the wait-queue entry embedded in a poll_iocb. Precondition: wait is the wait entry of the poll_iocb of a live aio_kiocb (iocb = container_of, ki_ctx valid); the caller (the waitqueue wake-up code) holds the wait queue head's lock; key is the poll key, converted with key_to_poll (a NULL key gives mask 0); mode and sync are unused. Exits: there are two return statements. (R1) If mask is non-zero and mask & req->events is 0 the function returns 0 and changes nothing. (R2) Otherwise it returns 1 after branch A or branch B. Branch A, taken when mask != 0 and req->work_scheduled is false and spin_trylock_irqsave(&ki_ctx->ctx_lock) succeeds: the wait entry is removed from the wait queue (list_del_init), the iocb is removed from the context's active list (list_del(&iocb->ki_list)), ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask); if iocb->ki_eventfd is set and eventfd_signal_allowed() is false, the local iocb pointer is set to NULL and req->work is re-initialised as aio_poll_put_work and scheduled (the iocb_put is then done by that work); ctx_lock is released with the saved flags; and if the local pointer is still set, iocb_put(iocb) is called after the lock is released. Branch B, taken otherwise (mask == 0, or work already scheduled, or the trylock failed): the wait entry stays on the queue unless POLLFREE is set; if req->work_scheduled is already true, req->work_need_resched = true, else schedule_work(&req->work) and req->work_scheduled = true; then, if (mask & POLLFREE), req->cancelled is set, the wait entry is removed from the queue (list_del_init) and, as the last step, req->head is set to NULL with smp_store_release. Branch B does not take ctx_lock and does not drop an iocb reference. POLLFREE is only handled specially in branch B; if branch A is taken for a mask containing POLLFREE the request is completed inline as for any other mask. No lock is held on return except the caller's own wait queue lock (the function acquires and releases ctx_lock only inside branch A).
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:1787-1867 and aio_poll_put_work at aio.c:1671-1677, key_to_poll at include/linux/wait.h:237 (NULL key gives 0). Changes from previous prose: the inline-branch condition now lists exactly 'mask && !req->work_scheduled && trylock' (1812-1813), both list removals are named (1816-1817), the two returns are named (1797, 1866), and the POLLFREE sentence is restricted to branch B (1853-1864) without 'always/never' wording.

name: aio_poll
prose: Function aio_poll(aiocb, iocb) (aio.c:1894-1967) starts an IOCB_CMD_POLL request. Precondition: aiocb is an initialised aio_kiocb (ki_ctx valid; the poll request's file pointer, which shares storage with ki_filp, is set); iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block; the caller holds no ctx_lock. Return statements: three. (R1) -EINVAL, before the poll request is touched, if (u16)iocb->aio_buf != iocb->aio_buf. (R2) -EINVAL, likewise, if aio_offset, aio_nbytes or aio_rw_flags is non-zero. (R3) the final 'return apt.error' (value 0 or -EINVAL). Otherwise: the work item is initialised to aio_poll_complete_work, req->events = demangle_poll(aio_buf) | EPOLLERR | EPOLLHUP, head is NULL, cancelled, work_scheduled and work_need_resched are false, the wait entry is initialised with aio_poll_wake, and apt.error starts as -EINVAL, apt.queued false. mask = vfs_poll(file, &apt.pt) & req->events (the queue callback adds the wait entry to the file's wait queue on its first call and records head, queued = true and error = 0; a second call leaves error = -EINVAL). Then ctx->ctx_lock is taken with interrupts disabled. Case 1, apt.queued false (the file registered no wait queue): the lock is dropped; if mask != 0, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), apt.error = 0 and iocb_put(aiocb) is called after the lock is released and the function returns 0 (completed synchronously); if mask == 0 it returns -EINVAL (the request is not queued anywhere and the caller keeps the reference and must destroy it). Case 2, apt.queued true: on_queue = poll_iocb_lock_wq(req), which is true only if req->head is non-NULL and the wait entry is still linked, in which case the wait queue head lock (and RCU read lock) is then held. If !on_queue or req->work_scheduled (aio_poll_wake already completed it or scheduled the completion work): if apt.error was non-zero (the file registered more than one wait queue) cancel is set; then apt.error = 0 and mask = 0. Next, if mask != 0 or apt.error != 0 (this can then only hold while on_queue is true and no work is scheduled): the wait entry is removed from the queue; else if cancel: req->cancelled is set (the iocb is not added to active_reqs); else if on_queue: the iocb is added to ctx->active_reqs and ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel; else nothing more is done. If on_queue the wait queue lock is released. After that, if mask != 0 (synchronous completion; the request is no longer on a wait queue, or was not on one to begin with): ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask) and apt.error = 0. ctx_lock is released; if mask != 0 iocb_put(aiocb) is called; the function returns apt.error. Result summary of case 2: it returns 0 when the request was completed synchronously (mask != 0 with no work scheduled and still on the queue), when it is waiting for an event (on the queue, no work scheduled, mask 0, one wait queue; now on active_reqs), when completion was already done or scheduled by aio_poll_wake (any mask ignored), and when more than one wait queue was registered but aio_poll_wake had already run (cancelled set); it returns -EINVAL when more than one wait queue was registered and the request was still on its first queue with no work scheduled and no event ready (the wait entry has been removed and the caller keeps the iocb reference), and it completes synchronously with return 0 when more than one wait queue was registered, the request was still on its queue with no work scheduled and mask != 0. ctx_lock and the wait queue lock are not held on any return.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived by enumerating every branch of aio.c:1894-1967 (returns at 1904, 1907, 1966; cases 1929-1958 and 1959-1965). Cross-checked: poll_iocb_lock_wq at aio.c:1695-1716 returns true only with head lock and RCU held (1707-1711); aio_poll_queue_proc at 1876-1892 sets queued/error; the earlier prose omitted the case where, with multiple wait queues and mask != 0 on an on-queue request, the request is completed synchronously (the 'mask || apt.error' branch at 1942 followed by 1959-1962). Language 'always/never' avoided; all exceptions listed.

name: __io_submit_one
prose: Function __io_submit_one(ctx, iocb, user_iocb, req, compat) (aio.c:1969-2021). Precondition: req is an aio_kiocb obtained from aio_get_req (so req->ki_eventfd is NULL and req->ki_refcnt is 2), iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block, user_iocb its user address, compat selects the compat layout. Return statements and effects, in order: (1) req->ki_filp = fget(iocb->aio_fildes); if that is NULL it returns -EBADF (no file reference held). (2) If IOCB_FLAG_RESFD is set in aio_flags, eventfd_ctx_fdget(aio_resfd) is called; on an error pointer it returns PTR_ERR of it (req->ki_filp holds a file reference, req->ki_eventfd stays NULL); on success req->ki_eventfd is set. (3) If put_user(KIOCB_KEY, &user_iocb->aio_key) fails it returns -EFAULT (req->ki_filp, and req->ki_eventfd if it was set, hold references). (4) Otherwise req->ki_res.obj = user_iocb address, data = iocb->aio_data, res = 0, res2 = 0, and the function returns the result of the handler selected by iocb->aio_lio_opcode: IOCB_CMD_PREAD aio_read(non-vectored), PWRITE aio_write(non-vectored), PREADV aio_read(vectored), PWRITEV aio_write(vectored), FSYNC aio_fsync(datasync false), FDSYNC aio_fsync(datasync true), POLL aio_poll(req, iocb); any other opcode returns -EINVAL. Each of those handlers returns 0 or a negative errno: aio_read and aio_write return 0 when the I/O was started or completed (an -EIOCBQUEUED from the file operation is absorbed by aio_rw_done and not returned), aio_fsync returns 0 after scheduling the work, or -EINVAL or -ENOMEM, aio_poll returns 0 or -EINVAL. This function itself neither releases the file reference nor the eventfd reference and does not touch ki_refcnt; on a non-zero return the caller io_submit_one drops one reference with iocb_put(req) and then calls iocb_destroy(req) (which puts the eventfd if set, fput on ki_filp if set, drops the context reqs reference and frees req) and put_reqs_available(ctx, 1); when the return is 0 the caller still drops one reference with iocb_put(req) and the request is completed, or will be completed asynchronously, with the remaining reference. No lock is taken or held by this function.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:1969-2021 and the callees aio_read/aio_write/aio_fsync (aio.c:1581-1669), aio_rw_done (1561-1579), iocb_destroy (1103-1111), aio_get_req (1054-1073: refcount_set(...,2), ki_eventfd = NULL) and io_submit_one (2053-2066). Earlier prose claimed the function 'does not itself release' references and that handlers 'never' return -EIOCBQUEUED; the latter is now stated with its reason (absorbed in aio_rw_done, 1563-1565, and the handlers' return values come from rw_verify_area/aio_prep_rw, 1589-1605, 1616-1637). Added the caller's iocb_put on both success and failure paths (2056).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit, aio_context_t, ctx_id, long, nr,
prose: System call io_submit(ctx_id, nr, iocbpp) (aio.c:2082-2121). Precondition: iocbpp is a user pointer to an array of nr user pointers to struct iocb; the call may sleep. Return statements: three. (R1) -EINVAL if nr < 0, before any lookup. (R2) -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) returns NULL (no reference was taken). (R3) the final 'return i ? i : ret', reached only after a reference on the context (ctx->users) was obtained by lookup_ioctx. On that path: nr is first reduced to ctx->nr_events if it is larger; if the reduced nr is greater than AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD a block plug is started and finished around the loop. For i = 0 .. nr-1 the loop reads the i-th iocb pointer with get_user (on a fault ret = -EFAULT and the loop stops) and calls io_submit_one(ctx, user_iocb, false); a non-zero result is stored in ret and stops the loop (ret is unchanged and stays 0 for a successful call). When the loop stops at index i, i iocbs were submitted successfully; if it runs to the end, i == nr. Then the plug is finished if it was started, the ctx->users reference is dropped (percpu_ref_put, line 2119), and the function returns i if i > 0, otherwise ret, which is the error that stopped the first iteration (-EFAULT from reading the pointer, or the error of io_submit_one, for example -EFAULT, -EINVAL, -EAGAIN, -EBADF or an error of the I/O handler), or 0 if no iocb was attempted (nr == 0 after the reduction). An error that occurs after at least one successful submission is not reported; only the count is returned.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2082-2121. Three returns (2091, 2096, 2120); loop stop conditions (2107-2114); single reference drop at 2119. Previous prose said the reference is dropped 'on every path after the lookup', which is true but is now stated as the single path at 2119; also dropped the vague 'the first error' wording by naming that a later error after i > 0 is not reported (2120).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel, aio_context_t, ctx_id, struct iocb __user *, iocb,
prose: System call io_cancel(ctx_id, iocb, result) (aio.c:2176-2216). Precondition: iocb is a user pointer to a control block previously passed to io_submit; result is not used by the function. Return statements: four. (R1) -EFAULT if get_user of iocb->aio_key faults. (R2) -EINVAL if the key is not KIOCB_KEY. (R3) -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) returns NULL (no context reference taken). (R4) the final 'return ret' after a context reference was obtained. On that path ret starts as -EINVAL; under ctx->ctx_lock (irq-disabling) the function walks ctx->active_reqs for the first entry whose ki_res.obj equals the user address of iocb; if one is found it calls its ki_cancel callback with the embedded kiocb, stores the callback's return value in ret, removes the entry from the list with list_del_init, and stops the search; if none is found ret stays -EINVAL. The lock is released. If ret is 0 it is replaced by -EINPROGRESS (the completion event, if any, is delivered through the ring and not through result); any other value, including a negative value from the callback, is returned unchanged. The ctx->users reference is dropped before the return. Nothing is written to result.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2176-2216: four returns (2186, 2188, 2192, 2215); search and callback at 2194-2202; the 0 -> -EINPROGRESS conversion at 2204-2211; reference drop at 2213. The earlier prose said a callback return other than 0 'is returned unchanged' which holds, now with the explicit statement that nothing is written to result.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents, aio_context_t, ctx_id,
prose: System call io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (aio.c:2251-2267, built only with CONFIG_64BIT). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event; timeout is NULL (wait without a time limit) or a user pointer to a struct __kernel_timespec holding a relative timeout; the call may sleep. Return statements: two. (R1) -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_timespec64 returns non-zero (it returns -EFAULT when the copy from user fails). (R2) the final 'return ret'. On that path ret (an int) is the value of do_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, ts or NULL), except that when that value is 0 and signal_pending(current) is true ret becomes -EINTR. do_io_getevents returns -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx finds no context (including when reading the ring id from user space faults), or, once a context reference was taken, if min_nr < 0 or min_nr > nr; otherwise it returns read_events(...): the number of events copied to the user buffer (this may be 0 or fewer than min_nr when the timeout expires or a signal interrupts the wait, since neither condition is turned into an error by read_events), or a negative errno only when no event had been copied yet: -EFAULT if a copy to the user buffer faulted (in that read of the ring the head is not advanced, so events of that read that were already copied remain in the ring), or -EINVAL if the context is dead. The context reference taken by do_io_getevents is dropped before it returns. io_getevents takes no locks of its own.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2251-2267 and callees do_io_getevents (2218-2235), read_events (1312-1367), aio_read_events (1295-1310), aio_read_events_ring (1218-1293; fault path 1271-1277 skips the head update at 1284-1286), lookup_ioctx (1075-1100) and get_timespec64 (kernel/time/time.c:872-891). Removed the earlier claim 'it fails only when the copy from user faults' as a guess about callers; now stated as the get_timespec64 contract read from source (only -EFAULT). Clarified that the unconsumed events after a fault include those already copied in that same ring read (the head is advanced once after the loop).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents
prose: System call io_pgetevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig) (aio.c:2276-2307). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event; timeout is NULL or a user pointer to a struct __kernel_timespec (relative); usig is NULL or a user pointer to a struct __aio_sigset {sigmask, sigsetsize}; the call may sleep. Return statements: four. (R1) -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_timespec64 fails. (R2) -EFAULT if usig is non-NULL and copy_from_user of the sigset descriptor fails (a NULL usig leaves ksig = {NULL, 0}). (R3) the non-zero result of set_user_sigmask(ksig.sigmask, ksig.sigsetsize), returned before any wait: set_user_sigmask returns 0 without changing anything when the mask pointer is NULL, -EINVAL when sigsetsize is not sizeof(sigset_t), -EFAULT when the mask cannot be copied; only on its success with a non-NULL mask does it save the current blocked mask in saved_sigmask, set the restore flag and install the new mask. (R4) the final 'return ret'. On that path ret = do_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, ts or NULL) (events copied, or -EINVAL for an unknown context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a negative errno from the ring read when no event had been copied yet); then interrupted = signal_pending(current); restore_saved_sigmask_unless(interrupted) restores the saved signal mask if a mask was installed and no signal is pending (if a signal is pending the mask is left to be restored when the signal is delivered); if interrupted and ret is 0, ret becomes -ERESTARTNOHAND; otherwise ret is returned as it is. The only conversion of ret is 0 to -ERESTARTNOHAND when a signal is pending; unlike io_getevents there is no -EINTR conversion, and a non-zero ret is returned unchanged.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2276-2307 and kernel/signal.c:3354-3370 (set_user_sigmask) and include/linux/sched/signal.h:571-577 (restore_saved_sigmask_unless). Four returns (2290, 2293, 2297, 2306). Earlier prose is kept in substance; added the exact set_user_sigmask contract (NULL mask returns 0) and the statement that no other conversion of ret happens.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents_time32, __u32, ctx_id,
prose: System call io_getevents_time32(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (aio.c:2349-2365, built with CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME). Parameters: ctx_id is a __u32 (zero-extended into the aio_context_t argument of do_io_getevents), min_nr and nr are __s32 (sign-extended to long), events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event, timeout is NULL (no time limit) or a user pointer to a struct old_timespec32 (relative). Return statements: two. (R1) -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_old_timespec32 returns non-zero. (R2) the final 'return ret'. On that path ret (an int) is the value of do_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, ts or NULL), except that when that value is 0 and signal_pending(current) is true ret becomes -EINTR. do_io_getevents returns -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx finds no context, or, after taking a context reference, if min_nr < 0 or min_nr > nr; otherwise it returns read_events(...): the number of events copied (possibly 0 or fewer than min_nr after a timeout or a signal, neither of which is turned into an error by read_events), or a negative errno only when no event had been copied yet (-EFAULT on a failed copy to the user buffer, -EINVAL if the context is dead). The context reference is dropped before it returns. No lock is taken by this function itself.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2349-2365 with do_io_getevents (2218-2235) and read_events (1312-1367). Two returns (2359, 2364). Added the parameter widths from the SYSCALL_DEFINE5 signature (__u32 ctx_id, __s32 min_nr and nr) and removed the claim that was previously implicit about the timeout copy failing only on a user fault (get_old_timespec32 result simply non-zero).

name: ceph_readdir
prose: Function ceph_readdir(file, ctx) (dir.c:317-639), the iterate_shared handler of a ceph directory. Precondition: file is an open directory whose private_data is its struct ceph_dir_file_info (dfi), ctx is a valid dir_context, no ceph spinlock is held by the caller. Return statements (all of them): (1) return 0 if CEPH_F_ATEND is set in dfi->file_info.flags. (2) return 0 if ctx->pos == 0 and dir_emit of '.' refuses; otherwise ctx->pos becomes 1. (3) return 0 if ctx->pos == 1 and dir_emit of '..' refuses; otherwise ctx->pos becomes 2. (4) return err if ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir(inode) returns a negative value (a non-negative return is ignored). (5) return err from __dcache_readdir, when the dcache path was taken and its result is not -EAGAIN. (6) return PTR_ERR(req) if ceph_mdsc_create_request fails. (7) return the error of ceph_alloc_readdir_reply_buffer after ceph_mdsc_put_request(req). (8) return -ENOMEM if kzalloc of r_path2 fails, after putting req. (9) return the negative result of ceph_encode_encrypted_dname, after putting req. (10) return the negative result of ceph_mdsc_do_request, after putting req. (11) return a non-zero result of note_last_dentry (-ENOMEM) after dropping dfi->last_readdir (put and set to NULL). (12) return -EIO, after dropping dfi->last_readdir (put and set to NULL), when a buffered entry has rde->offset < ctx->pos (dir.c:545-552). (13) return -EIO, after dropping dfi->last_readdir, when a buffered entry has no inode (rde->inode.in is NULL; 554-558). (14) return 0 when dir_emit refuses a buffered entry, with ctx->pos equal to that entry's offset and dfi->last_readdir kept (not put) so the next call resumes from it. (15) the final return 0. Behaviour. The dcache path (when the mount options have DCACHE and not NOASYNCREADDIR, the inode is not the snapshot dir, the directory is complete and ordered, and the shared file cap is issued) calls __dcache_readdir; only an -EAGAIN result falls through to the normal path. Before that, the write file mode is touched under i_ceph_lock. Normal path, label more: if need_send_readdir (no dfi->last_readdir, or the buffered frag does not cover ctx->pos) the old reply, if any, is put and set to NULL, a READDIR (or LSSNAP for the snapshot dir) request to the auth MDS is built for the frag (taken from ctx->pos, or chosen by ceph_choose_frag for hash order) with r_path2 holding the encoded last name when dfi->last_name is set, and sent; if the reply names another frag, dfi->frag is updated and, unless the reply is hash ordered, ctx->pos is set to the start of that frag. The reply is stored in dfi->last_readdir; the readdir-cache and dir_release_count bookkeeping is updated depending on CEPH_MDS_R_DID_PREPOPULATE; if the reply has entries note_last_dentry records the last name and the next offset (2 when dir_end), and if it has none but dir_end, next_offset = 2. Emission: a binary search over dir_entries (assuming ascending offsets) finds the first entry whose offset is >= ctx->pos, so entries with a smaller offset at the front of the buffer are skipped silently without error; for each entry from there on ctx->pos is set to the entry offset before dir_emit and incremented after a successful emit, and an entry whose offset is below the current ctx->pos (for example one that does not increase) makes the function return -EIO as listed in (12). When all buffered entries have been emitted the reply is put and dfi->last_readdir set to NULL; if dfi->next_offset > 2 the same frag is requested again (goto more); otherwise, if the frag is not the rightmost, the next frag is selected: for hash order ctx->pos is raised to the position of the next frag when that is larger, otherwise ctx->pos is set to the start of the next frag and dfi->last_name is freed and set to NULL; then goto more. At the end of the last frag CEPH_F_ATEND is set; if i_release_count equals dfi->dir_release_count, then under i_ceph_lock, if dfi->dir_ordered_count also equals i_ordered_count i_size is set to readdir_cache_idx * sizeof(struct dentry *) (a BUG_ON requires readdir_cache_idx >= 0 in that case), and in both cases __ceph_dir_set_complete(ci, dfi->dir_release_count, dfi->dir_ordered_count) records the directory as complete with those counts; then it returns 0. No ceph spinlock is held at any return. A reply kept in dfi->last_readdir stays there on returns (1) to (5) (they come before this call touches it) and on return (14); on returns (6) to (13) it has been put and set to NULL, or no reply was stored.
note: Reviewer claim (annotation says an offset below ctx->pos returns -EIO; code skips such entries): PARTLY RIGHT, but the -EIO behaviour is real. fs/ceph/dir.c:545-552: inside the emit loop 'if (rde->offset < ctx->pos) { pr_warn_client(...); ceph_mdsc_put_request(dfi->last_readdir); dfi->last_readdir = NULL; return -EIO; }'. What the reviewer saw as 'skip' is the binary search at 530-541 which advances i past leading entries with offset < ctx->pos before the loop starts, silently. So both behaviours exist: leading smaller entries are skipped (530-541), a smaller offset met inside the loop returns -EIO (545-552). The previous prose only said -EIO; the new prose states both. Other points verified from the source and fixed: complete marking always calls __ceph_dir_set_complete in both branches (632-633), only the ordered branch writes i_size (625-627); the full list of returns (333, 341, 355, 361, 378, 411, 416, 431, 438, 459, 515, 551, 557, 575, 638); the hash-order versus non-hash-order next-frag handling (593-604).

name: static inline void ecryptfs_release_messaging(void)
prose: This is the static inline stub ecryptfs_release_messaging(void) at ecryptfs_kernel.h:612-613, inside the #else branch (line 607) of '#ifdef CONFIG_ECRYPT_FS_MESSAGING' (line 598), so it is the definition seen only when CONFIG_ECRYPT_FS_MESSAGING is not defined. When that option is defined the header only declares 'void ecryptfs_release_messaging(void);' (line 606) and the real function is defined in messaging.c, which is not part of this item and is not described here. Precondition: none (the function has no parameters). Postcondition: the body is empty ('{ }'): it returns nothing, reads and writes no data, and takes or releases no lock, reference or memory. There is exactly one exit, the end of the empty body.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Checked against fs/ecryptfs/ecryptfs_kernel.h:598-612 (stub inside the #else branch, empty body) and fs/ecryptfs/messaging.c:420-455 (the real function, which frees the message context array, the daemon hash and destroys the miscdev; deliberately not attributed to the stub). The prose now states which configuration the stub belongs to and that the real function exists separately.

name: v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl
prose: The function in this item is v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl(dir, dentry, file, flags, omode) (vfs_inode_dotl.c:226-337), the atomic_open inode operation of 9P2000.L directories (the function named v9fs_vfs_create_dotl at line 220 is a different 3-line function that just returns v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(idmap, dir, dentry, omode, 0)). The slice starts at line 252, in the middle of it, so lines 242-250 are before the slice. Precondition: dir is a directory inode on a 9p mount, dentry names the entry to open in it, file is the struct file being opened, omode is the creation mode; the function may sleep. Result: an int; it returns 0 on success or a negative errno. Return statements: three. Before the slice start (lines 242-250): if d_in_lookup(dentry) is true the function calls v9fs_vfs_lookup(dir, dentry, 0); if that returns a non-NULL result or leaves the dentry positive, return 1 is finish_no_open(file, res) (line 245), which is defined in fs/open.c:1072-1078 as 'if (IS_ERR(dentry)) return PTR_ERR(dentry); file->__f_path.dentry = dentry; return 0;', so it returns 0 here and not 1; nothing is created. Return 2 (line 250): if flags does not have O_CREAT set, it returns finish_no_open(file, NULL), i.e. 0 with a NULL dentry stored in file, and nothing is created; there is no -ENOENT return and no finish_no_open(file, dentry) in this function. Return 3 (line 336), the common exit 'out', is reached with err = 0 or a negative errno after the creation steps in the slice, as follows. It takes v9ses from dir, then dfid = v9fs_parent_fid(dentry) (error: goto out), ofid = clone_fid(dfid) (error: goto out), gid = v9fs_get_fsgid_for_create(dir), mode = omode adjusted by v9fs_acl_mode (error: goto out; it also returns the default and access ACLs dacl and pacl), then, if the session has CACHE_WRITEBACK and p9_omode has P9_OWRITE, the write-only open is replaced by read-write without P9_DOTL_APPEND; then err = p9_client_create_dotl(ofid, name, p9_omode, mode, gid, &qid) (a negative result goes to out; from this point the file exists on the server even if a later step fails); v9fs_invalidate_inode_attr(dir); fid = p9_client_walk(dfid, 1, &name, 1) (error: goto out); inode = v9fs_get_new_inode_from_fid(v9ses, fid, dir->i_sb) (error: goto out, with fid still owned here); v9fs_set_create_acl(inode, fid, dacl, pacl); v9fs_fid_add(dentry, &fid) hands fid to the dentry and sets the local fid to NULL; d_instantiate(dentry, inode); err = finish_open(file, dentry, generic_file_open) (a non-zero result goes to out, after the dentry has already been instantiated with the new inode). On success it sets file->private_data = ofid, with CONFIG_9P_FSCACHE and CACHE_FSCACHE calls fscache_use_cookie for the inode's cookie, calls v9fs_fid_add_modes(ofid, ...), v9fs_open_fid_add(inode, &ofid) (adds ofid to the inode's open-fid list and sets the local ofid to NULL), and sets FMODE_CREATED in file->f_mode. At out, p9_fid_put is called on dfid, ofid and fid (each call is a no-op for a NULL or error pointer; a fid handed over above is already NULL), v9fs_put_acl(dacl, pacl) releases the ACL references, and err is returned. dfid is not handed over to anything, so it is dropped at out; ofid and fid are dropped there only if they were not handed over (a handed-over one is NULL).
note: Reviewer claim (prose says O_CREAT unset returns finish_no_open(file, NULL); code returns -ENOENT or finish_no_open(file, dentry)): WRONG. fs/9p/vfs_inode_dotl.c:249-250 reads 'if (!(flags & O_CREAT)) return finish_no_open(file, NULL);' and there is no -ENOENT in the function (the only returns are 245, 250, 336). The reviewer was working from the slice that starts at line 252, which does not contain lines 242-250 at all; the prose now says explicitly that lines 242-250 precede the slice and quotes them. Other fixes: finish_no_open (fs/open.c:1072-1078) returns PTR_ERR(dentry) for an error pointer, so the first return is 'finish_no_open(file, res)' and not simply 0; p9_fid_put ignores NULL and error pointers (include/net/9p/client.h:269-272); v9fs_fid_add and v9fs_open_fid_add set the caller's pointer to NULL (fs/9p/fid.c:33-42, 93-102). The dentry is instantiated at 313-314, before finish_open at 317, so only a finish_open failure leaves an instantiated dentry.

name: ext4_ext_insert_extent
prose: The function in this item is ext4_ext_insert_extent(handle, inode, path, newext, gb_flags) (extents.c:1997-2221); the slice starts at line 2046, in the middle of it (the text '(tail; name elided in excerpt)' is not part of the name; the lines before the slice, 1997-2045, hold the argument checks and the PRE_IO guard described below). Precondition: handle is an active journal handle with enough credits; path is the extent-tree path from ext4_find_extent for newext's logical block, valid down to the leaf at ext_depth(inode); newext points to the extent to insert, whose block range does not overlap an existing extent; gb_flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags. Result: a struct ext4_ext_path pointer, or an error pointer. Return statements: three, all of them at or after line 2140, so inside the slice or at its end. (R1) 'return path' at 2140 when ext4_ext_create_new_leaf returns an error pointer. (R2) 'return path' at 2216 on success. (R3) 'return ERR_PTR(err)' at 2220, after errout frees the current path, the one passed in or its replacement (ext4_free_ext_path). The function behaves as follows. Before the slice (file lines 1997-2045, not shown in it, not additional returns): if gb_flags has DELALLOC_RESERVE, mb_flags gets EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED; if the actual length of newext is 0, EXT4_ERROR_INODE is reported and err = -EFSCORRUPTED, then 'goto errout' (lines 2010-2013); if path[depth].p_hdr is NULL, the same err and goto errout (2018-2022); errout is the label at line 2218 that frees the path and returns ERR_PTR(err), which is the (R3) return. Then, at line 2025, 'if (ex && !(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO))' guards the whole neighbour-merge block (the lines in this slice from 2046 on up to 2096 are inside it): when gb_flags has EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO, or when there is no nearest extent ex, this block is skipped entirely, i.e. neither the append nor the prepend merge is tried. Inside the block (the part visible in this slice from 2046): ex is first moved to its right neighbour (when it is not the last extent and ends before newext, then 'goto prepend') or left neighbour (when it is not the first extent and newext ends before it); then, if ext4_can_extents_be_merged(inode, ex, newext), the extent is appended: ext4_ext_get_access (error: errout), ex->ee_len grows by newext's length keeping the unwritten mark, nearex = ex, goto merge; else at prepend:, if ext4_can_extents_be_merged(inode, newext, ex), ext4_ext_get_access (error: errout), ex takes newext's block and physical block and grows by newext's length keeping the unwritten mark, nearex = ex, goto merge. If no merge was done or the block was skipped: depth and eh are re-read; if the leaf has room (eh_entries < eh_max) goto has_space. Otherwise the next leaf is tried when newext's block is above the last extent of this leaf and ext4_ext_next_leaf_block gives a block: ext4_find_extent(inode, next, NULL, gb_flags) (error: err goes to errout), BUG_ON on a depth mismatch, and if that leaf has room the old path is freed (ext4_free_ext_path) and the new path replaces it (goto has_space), else the new path is freed. If still no room: with gb_flags METADATA_NOFAIL mb_flags gets EXT4_MB_USE_RESERVED, and path = ext4_ext_create_new_leaf(...) (an error pointer is returned directly as R1; that function frees the path itself on failure); depth and eh are re-read. has_space: nearex = path[depth].p_ext; ext4_ext_get_access (error: errout); with no extent in the leaf nearex is the first slot; otherwise nearex is advanced by one if newext's block is above nearex's block (BUG_ON equal blocks otherwise) and the entries from there to the end of the leaf are moved up by one slot with memmove; eh_entries is incremented, path[depth].p_ext = nearex and the block, physical block and length of newext are stored in it. merge: when gb_flags does not have PRE_IO, ext4_ext_try_to_merge(handle, inode, path, nearex) is called (no result); then ext4_ext_correct_indexes (error: errout) and ext4_ext_dirty on path + path->p_depth (error: errout); then R2. With gb_flags PRE_IO therefore both the append/prepend merge (line 2025) and ext4_ext_try_to_merge (line 2204) are skipped. On success the returned path is the one passed in or, if the next leaf or a new leaf was used, a different path that replaces it; the caller owns the returned path. On an error return the caller gets only the error pointer and must not use the path it passed in, because it was freed by this function, or by ext4_ext_create_new_leaf or ext4_find_extent on their failures. When a late step (index correction or dirtying) fails, the in-memory leaf may already contain the change.
note: Reviewer claim (PRE_IO does not skip append/prepend merging; only ext4_ext_try_to_merge is skipped): WRONG. fs/ext4/extents.c:2025 'if (ex && !(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO)) {' opens the block that contains both the append attempt (2047-2067) and the prepend attempt (2069-2095) and closes at 2096, so with PRE_IO neither is tried; and 2204 'if (!(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO)) ext4_ext_try_to_merge(...)' separately skips the post-insert merge. The slice given to the reviewer begins at line 2046, after the guard at 2025, so the guard was not visible; the prose now states the guard with its line number. Other points verified: three returns (2140, 2216, 2220); ext4_ext_create_new_leaf frees the path on its own failures (extents.c:1460-1462 and ext4_find_extent's err label at 970-972); the early errors -EFSCORRUPTED at 2010-2013 and 2018-2022 are before the slice.

name: afs_select_vlserver
prose: Function afs_select_vlserver(vc) (vl_rotate.c:93-319): selects the next volume location server and address to try, and may be called repeatedly. Precondition: vc was set up by afs_begin_vlserver_operation (nr_iterations starts at -1); on calls after the first, vc->alist is the address list used by the previous call, vc->addr_index indexes the address tried, and vc->call_error, vc->call_abort_code and vc->call_responded hold the outcome of the previous call; the cursor is used by one task at a time. Return statements: four. (R1) return false at line 111 if AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is already set. (R2) return false at line 127 when the previous call's error is 0 or any error not listed below. (R3) return true at line 278 when an address has been selected. (R4) return false at line 318, the end of label failed. In every case vc->nr_iterations is incremented first (line 102), before the STOP test. Control flow. (R1): no other change. First call (nr_iterations == 0 after the increment): goto start. Later calls: last_error of alist->addrs[vc->addr_index] is set to call_error, then call_error selects: 0 or any unlisted error: cumul_error.error = error, AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is set, R2; the alist and server_list references stay in the cursor. -ECONNABORTED: with abort code AFSVL_IO, AFSVL_BADVOLOPER or AFSVL_NOMEM, afs_prioritise_error(cumul_error, -EREMOTEIO, abort_code) and goto next_server; with any other abort code, afs_prioritise_error(cumul_error, error, abort_code) and goto failed. -ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME: afs_prioritise_error(cumul_error, error, 0) and goto iterate_address. -ECONNRESET: the same recording, AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY is set, goto next_server. -EOPNOTSUPP: goto next_server with no error recorded. Label next_server: if vc->call_responded, vc->addr_index != alist->preferred and the bit alist->preferred is set in vc->addr_tried, alist->preferred is set to vc->addr_index; the alist reference is put (afs_put_addrlist) and both alist and vc->alist become NULL; then pick_server. Label restart_from_beginning (reached only from no_more_servers when RETRY is set): it tests vc->call_responded and, when that is true, evaluates vc->alist->preferred although vc->alist is NULL on the only path that reaches this label, from no_more_servers (it was cleared at next_server before pick_server), so with call_responded true this line dereferences a NULL pointer; when call_responded is false, afs_put_addrlist(NULL) does nothing; the server list reference is put and vc->server_list set to NULL; if AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRIED is already set goto failed, else RETRIED is set and control falls into start. Label start: afs_start_vl_iteration(vc); if it returns false goto failed. That function may wait interruptibly for a DNS lookup (a signal sets cumul_error.error = -ERESTARTSYS), sets -ENOENT if DNS reports the cell as not found, -EDESTADDRREQ if no DNS record is available, and otherwise takes a reference on the cell's server list into vc->server_list; if that list has no servers it returns false without setting an error (the reference stays held), else it sets untried_servers to one bit per server and server_index = -1. Then afs_send_vl_probes (an error < 0 is recorded with afs_prioritise_error and goes to failed), then pick_server. Label pick_server: afs_wait_for_vl_probes (an error < 0 is recorded and goes to failed); server_index = server_list->preferred; if that bit is still set in untried_servers goto selected_server (the preferred server is chosen without checking that it responded); otherwise the untried server with AFS_VLSERVER_FL_RESPONDING set and the lowest probe rtt is chosen, the last one among equal rtts; if none exists goto no_more_servers. Label selected_server: its bit is cleared in untried_servers, vc->server is set, the server's address list is read under its lock and a reference taken into vc->alist, vc->addr_tried = 0, vc->addr_index = -1, falling into iterate_address. Label iterate_address: the candidate set is alist->responded minus alist->probe_failed minus vc->addr_tried; if it is empty goto next_server; vc->addr_index is alist->preferred if that bit is in the set, else the lowest set bit; that bit is set in vc->addr_tried, vc->alist = alist, vc->call_responded = false, and R3 returns true. Label no_more_servers: if AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY is set goto restart_from_beginning; otherwise for each server in the list cumul_error.responded is set when it is RESPONDING and its probe error and abort code are merged with afs_prioritise_error, then fall into failed. Label failed: if alist is non-NULL the preferred address is updated as in next_server, the reference is put and alist and vc->alist become NULL; AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is set and R4 returns false; vc->server_list stays referenced (it is NULL only after restart_from_beginning put it and start did not reload it) for afs_end_vlserver_operation, and the final error is in vc->cumul_error.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed), prose rebuilt from the full control flow of fs/afs/vl_rotate.c:93-319 plus afs_start_vl_iteration (42-87). Four returns (111, 127, 278, 318); eight labels. Corrections to the earlier text: (1) the earlier prose said the preferred-address update happens when 'the last call responded on a different address whose preferred address was tried'; the code tests call_responded, addr_index != alist->preferred, and the preferred bit in addr_tried (283-286, 309-312, 174-177); (2) the earlier prose omitted that the preferred server is picked without a responding check (210-212); (3) restart_from_beginning (172-185) reads vc->alist->preferred when vc->call_responded is true although vc->alist was set to NULL at 288 before pick_server (the only path in is no_more_servers at 295-296); this is an apparent NULL dereference in the source and is stated as such, not hidden; call_responded is set from the call outcome in fs/afs/vlclient.c:155, 304, 667, 785, so it can be true; (4) after the first-call 'start' path the server_list reference is held on every false return that follows afs_start_vl_iteration taking it (including the empty-list case, 81-82).
